erin: FYI apiserver error-rate jump in eu-central starting 2024-05-20T09:33:19Z. Controller-manager liveness failing, several apiserver pods reporting `504 upstream timeout`. Looks correlated with a GPU fleet attach wave from 09:32+.
vik: Seeing huge SYN_RECV counts on NATs; ephemeral port exhaustion predicted. netstat shows many CONN_STATE_ESTABLISHED -> TIME_WAIT for short-lived attach flows.
raj: Etcd leader reports high wal fsync latency at 09:33:25 (p95 ~1.2s). Follower replication lagging, leader steps down briefly. apiserver clientv3 errors: `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed`.
net-bot: Alert: NAT ephemeral ports low (eu-central-nat-3 95% used) at 09:34:01. Suggested mitigation: reduce outbound fanout or add SNAT capacity.
erin: Controller-manager OOM observed on ctrl-nodes: reconciler-worker used 2.1GB vs request 1.5GB when listing pods across the new nodes. Restart loops started 09:34:10.
vik: Quick mitigation plan: 1) pause GPU attach concurrency, 2) mark new nodes cordoned to stop pod churn, 3) bump conntrack and ephemeral port range on NATs, 4) route less-critical read traffic to eu-west.
raj: I can push a small etcd compaction delay until the burst finishes; compaction at this time increases IO and competes with wal fsync. Will hold compaction start by adding `--compaction-interval` jitter.
erin: Applying temporary patch to autoscaler: `kubectl -n infra exec deploy/gpu-autoscaler -- bash -lc "export MAX_CONCURRENT_ATTACH=6; pkill -HUP autoscaler"` (temp). Also cordoning new node pool: `kubectl label nodes pool-gpu-new node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=true`.
infra-team: We opened CLOUD-10377 to provision additional SNAT IPs. Also running `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=230000` on nat-3.
k8s-bot: Observed: apiserver 5xx rate dropped from 4.8% to 0.9% after throttling and SNAT bump (09:40 UTC). Controller-manager restarts reduced.\avnote: Note: ephemeral port exhaustion often shows as `connect: cannot assign requested address` on apiserver logs; check `ip_local_port_range` and per-node SNAT allocation for heavy attach workloads.
vik: For long-term: consider per-node SNAT allocations (EIPs), BPF-based NAT to avoid conntrack scaling issues, autoscaler rate-limits tied to `apiserver_5xx` and `etcd_commit_latency`, and increase ctrlmgr memory requests for large reconciles. Also evaluate spreading attach spikes with token-bucket smoothing.
erin: Action items: raj to schedule compaction window movement + add jitter, vik to author autoscaler smoothing PR, infra-team to evaluate per-node EIP pools and SNAT cost estimate, ops to update runbook with new alert thresholds.
raj: Collecting logs and metrics now; will upload to ticket CLOUD-10377 and ping when ready.
erin: Thanks all. Will leave thread open until postmortem draft is in. :+1:
